about.text: Kheer is a sweet rice pudding of the Indian subcontinent, made by boiling milk, sugar or jaggery and rice together and flavoured with cardamom, saffron, nuts and dried fruit. Its name comes from Sanskrit kshira, milk, and it is a staple temple offering.

how.text: Rice is cooked slowly in milk, which thickens as it reduces and as the starch swells; sugar and spice go in towards the end. The Wikipedia page gives no temperatures or times, so none are listed.

steps.note: Rice, or cracked wheat, vermicelli, sago or tapioca in some versions, is cooked slowly in the milk until it thickens.
Sugar or jaggery, with cardamom, saffron, almonds and raisins, towards the end.
